title: While everyone is vibecoding an MMO, I'm making the first Massively Single Player RPG - World of Yooze where every player is an instance of You
author: re-skob
selftext:
I had a little prototype I made of this awhile back that was super basic ascii art, and I wanted to test Fable and GPT 5.6 so I resurrected it to give it a graphical overhaul and fix a bunch of bugs.

Fable is a huge token eater, so I use it as a "Lead Engineer" and primary orchestrator and have it spin up subagents with Codex CLI since OpenAI is a lot more generous with their tokens and does a great job when given explicit instructions, while Fable seems to have more "taste"

Then I just continued on exclusively in Codex because it can use its image gen tool to flesh out the art.

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: I'm trying to figure out how to do what you did, with having Fable be lead design, an instance of GPT Sol as lead engineer, and terra as grunt.  Is this possible?  How do I do this?

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body:
Claude Code is particularly good at splitting up the work, creating subagents and having them all work independently and then figuring out how to bring all of the worktrees together and resolve any merge conflicts. So I have it use that functionality in /batch mode but tell it to use codex cli instead of spinning up its own subagents using Fable model which just eats tokens. 

Codex isn't very good at creating subagents with different models, though, so once you do a request with Sol, it's just gonna keep using Sol.

I use terra only when I have very little individual requests (ie: flip this sprite, do some tuning) where it doesn't have to think too much, just mutate some files.

comments.author: ShiftyShankerton
comments.body: I'm tired of all these pixel art games lol. You're using AI yet you pick dated graphics.

replies.author: Low_Veterinarian6840
replies.body:
I definitely get what you're saying, but pixel art these days is an artistic choice, it's not about dated graphics. Again, definitely a personal preference! I think pixel art will always be around no matter what, there's a decent amount of people that love the nostalgia and vibe of it. Using AI for gamedev doesn't necessarily mean that everything has to be gorgeous, or the most high fidelity graphics, it's there to assist you with any kind of project you'd like to do. And for this one, the dev wanted a pixel art style. :)

I think too that AI making gorgeous pixel art is impressive too. Years ago, I wasn't able to make the same sprites that models could create today. Pixel art requires this kind of creative abstraction, and it's neat that models are starting to get better at it.

comments.author: Agreeable-Safety-360
comments.body: How did  you get all of your UI  to be consistent. Share the goods about what you did.

replies.author: YYY003003
replies.body: Yeah. I want to learn about that too.

replies.author: bettertagsweretaken
replies.body: Always start with a coherent at direction and prompt from there. You have to know what you want to see when the prompting completes.

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: start with a skeleton with boxes on where everything goes, then create a single sheet with all of your basic UI components - panel borders, buttons, icons, etc and reuse them as much as possible. Create new ones when necessary using the original sheet as the reference point

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: you play through the game (builder rpg type, kill monsters, collect resources, craft items) when you die you create a new character but your old character that got killed plays through the game as you did, so everything your old character has done gets persisted in the world as you go and continue doing other stuff with your old character.
